narr: Scattered to numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms developed throughout the day on June 5th, ahead of a stationary cut off upper low pressure system over Central Texas. Daytime heating contributed to moderate instability within a very moist air mass in place. These showers and thunderstorms were very efficient rainfall producers as they moved slowly and often trained over the same areas over a given period of time. Showers and thunderstorms containing heavy rainfall developed over much of Panola County during the late afternoon through the evening, with widespread rainfall amounts of 4-8 inches falling over this area. These amounts fell over already saturated grounds from heavy rainfall which fell a day prior, with two day totals of 6-12 inches observed. This resulted in widespread flash flooding across Southern and Eastern Panola County, where multiple roads were covered in high rushing water, including Highway 59 just south of Carthage. These showers and isolated thunderstorms finally diminished during the late evening hours.
